title: Microsoft Teams: change the background while recording a video clip on iPhone
summary: Hold: the admin path omits the Edit action required to reach the messaging policy settings. The briefing also incorrectly says the roadmap does not use the name video clip, although its description explicitly does.

claims.where: summary; controls[0].governs; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Scope
claims.claim: The Video messages messaging policy setting controls whether users can send video messages in chats and channels.
claims.quote: Video messages - Turn this setting on if you want users in your organization to be able to use the Teams app to send video messages to other people in chats and channels.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Sending video clips falls within the video messages capability governed by the messaging policy.
claims.quote: Record video messages directly from within a Teams chat using Video clips.: Video clip is a new feature in Microsoft Teams that enables the user to record, review, send, and view short-form video in Teams chat from desktop and mobile.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Teams admin center > Messaging policies > policy > Video messages is the path to edit the setting.
claims.quote: Select the policy by clicking to the left of the policy name, and then select Edit.
claims.fix: Replace controls[0].ui.path and the rendered table path with 'Messaging policies > policy > Edit > Video messages'. The cited page requires selecting Edit after selecting the policy.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMessagingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowVideoMessages $true enables video messages in the specified policy.
claims.quote: This setting determines if users can create and send video messages. Possible values: True, False

claims.where: controls[0].scope; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: Messaging policies are assigned to users, so different users can have different messaging policy settings.
claims.quote: You can assign a policy directly to users, either individually or at scale through a batch assignment (if supported for the policy type), or to a group that the users are members of (if supported for the policy type).

claims.where: Scope
claims.claim: Users automatically receive the global messaging policy unless a custom policy is created and assigned.
claims.quote: Users in your organization will automatically get the global policy, unless you create and assign a custom policy.

claims.where: Governance controls
claims.claim: A user can be assigned only one messaging policy at a time.
claims.quote: A user can only be assigned one messaging policy at a time.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Teams does not screen images users upload as meeting backgrounds.
claims.quote: Teams doesn't screen the images your users upload.

claims.where: Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Participants can use video effects is documented as controlling video background customization in meetings.
claims.quote:
Participants can use video effects

This is a per-user policy. This setting controls whether users can customize their video background in a meeting.

claims.where: Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Whether meeting video effects or customization policies govern clip backgrounds is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "recording" "background" "clip" "policy". Opened Meeting policy settings for audio & video and IT Admins- Manage and create custom meeting backgrounds for Teams meetings; neither states that these policies apply to clips.

claims.where: Governance controls
claims.claim: Learn does not document a control for the clip background option itself.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "recording" "background" "clip" "policy". Opened messaging policies, Set-CsTeamsMessagingPolicy, audio & video meeting policies, and custom meeting backgrounds; no clip-background control.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Scope; Open questions
claims.claim: The arrival default of the clip background option is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams video clip background recording iOS on by default admin setting. Read roadmap, Manage messaging policies in Teams, Government Channel release notes, and Meeting policy settings for audio & video; none states this option's arrival default.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a licensing requirement specifically for changing a background while recording a clip.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "video clip" "license". Opened Teams service description and custom meeting backgrounds; read Teams Premium licensing excerpts. No clip-background entitlement was stated.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No feature-specific price or meter for clip background changes is published in the sources found.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams video clips change background recording license premium pricing. Opened Teams service description and messaging policies; read Teams Premium licensing and Teams interoperability pricing excerpts. No clip-background price or meter.

claims.where: Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The Learn page describing Video messages lists no licensing requirement for that setting.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "video messages" "licensing" "background". Opened and read Manage messaging policies in Teams in full; its Video messages entry specifies sending in chats and channels without naming a licence.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: No identity or sign-in change is described for this clip background feature.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams record video clip change background mobile iOS identity sign-in background screening policy. Read roadmap, messaging policies, meeting audio & video policies, and Teams sign-in excerpt; no identity change for this feature.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The roadmap describes user recording and sharing, not an autonomous action.
claims.quote: You can record a video clip with your phone camera and switch your background to any picture you want or make it blurry. With this feature, you can record yourself anywhere and share it with coworkers in your Teams chat or channel.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The messaging policy page describes sending video messages without naming video clips or their background option.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "video clips" "AllowVideoMessages". Opened and read Manage messaging policies in Teams in full; the Video messages entry names chats and channels but not video clips or clip backgrounds.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Equivalent image screening or background policy enforcement for clips remains undocumented.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams video clip background screening uploaded images policy. Opened Meeting policy settings for audio & video and custom meeting backgrounds; their screening and background-policy statements concern meetings, not clips.
